output.answer: Eviction pops keys off the front of the `order` queue and removes them from `map`, but it removes more than asked — `evict_oldest(n)` drops up to n+1 entries and `put` inflates n by one more — and because `order` can hold stale duplicates of a re-inserted key, a pop can delete an entry that is still current.

claims.text: evict_oldest removes entries by popping the front of the `order` VecDeque and deleting that key from `map`, so it removes whole key/value pairs in insertion order.
Despite the doc comment saying it evicts `n` entries, the loop is `for _ in 0..=n`, which iterates n+1 times and therefore pops up to n+1 entries.
put() computes `overflow = map.len() - max_entries` and calls `evict_oldest(overflow + 1)`, so at the boundary (overflow == 0) it asks for 1 and the inclusive loop actually removes 2 entries.

put() pushes the key onto `order` on every call without removing any earlier occurrence, so re-inserting an existing key leaves a stale duplicate in the queue; eviction popping that stale entry removes the key from `map` even though the newer insert of the same key is still live.
Eviction removes nothing beyond the map entry itself — `hits` is never adjusted, and `map.remove` does not purge other occurrences of the key remaining in `order`.
